section.ground: #F2EBDD (cream, full colour; no verse grade). Frames and rings from the logo palette in render/hp/kand_e.html: #B31B1B red, #2346FF blue, #F2C300 yellow, #FF2E88 pink, #7B3FF2 violet, #15131F ink. Body text #0E0D12 on cream or yellow; red #B31B1B on the key word.

notes: Four bars, one item per bar, each item starts on its bar line (42.493, 44.42, 46.37, 48.298). Each sung line starts at a whisper time 0.2 to 0.4 s before its bar (42.3, 44.04, 46.06, 48.04), and whisper times run early, so the bar line is the entry point. Hand-off: v1b's last item (exploited, 40.542 to 42.493) ends on the same frame this section begins, so the verse-dark ground cuts to cream on 42.493 with one-frame white flash. The explicit word 'fucking' sits at 44.88 to 45.22, inside item 2. No visual event is tied to it, so the clean audio variant needs no picture change. Song lyrics appear on screen nowhere in this section. Clip speech is muted during every sung bar (42.493 to 50.225 is all sung vocal), so item 3 is the only clip and it is muted with a pull-quote in the with-song cut and audible only in the no-song cut. Item 1 (~17,600): hf-timeline.png was opened and its chart labels are too small to read at phone width, so the number is set as a card with the verbatim sentence, and the chart is provenance only. Item 2: the Guardian headline was checked against the local screenshot (exact match, including curly apostrophe and quotes). It is 80 characters over 1.93 s (about 41 characters per second), so the fallback trims with a leading ellipsis to '…CEO declares ‘golden age’'. Item 3: the speaker was checked on a reference frame at 452.8 s (the guest in the Daily Show guest chair is speaking). The transcript places the words at 452.24 to 454.26 and the sentence before them ('they saw the thing poking its head out of the sandbox') gives the context for 'did it again'. coxon-lines.json labels this line Jacob Coxon. The same file labels 'So, I heard you talking about jobs' (522.04) as Jon Stewart, which conflicts with the README and SUMMARY. That line is not used here, so it stays unresolved and item 3 does not depend on it. Item 4: the 19% is the paper's counterfactual gap for ages 22 to 25 in AI-exposed occupations. The 0.8 headcount level on the chart is a different number and must not share the screen with 19%. The paper calls the effect descriptive, not causal, so the stamp must not say AI caused it.
